text:
Maria Support: Hi all — escalating a customer (Acme) issue hitting our embeddings endpoint. They flipped quant_profile to `int8` and started getting 384-length vectors from what should be a 768-d model. Their downstream join fails with dimension errors and they reported higher latency + intermittent 5xx during batching.

Devon Eng: can you paste the exact request they sent (model id, quant_profile, headers + payload)?

Maria Support: Sanitzed request from ticket: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "open-embed-768-v1",
  "input": ["query1","query2"],
  "quant_profile": "int8",
  "batch_size": 64
}
```
They included a single response body showing a shorter vector: 
```
{"object":"embedding","embedding":[... 384 floats ...],"model":"open-embed-768-v1-int8"}
```
They said that before switching to `int8` (they used `fp16`) they consistently got 768-d vectors.

Jules ML: that should not alter dimension. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) router returned a different model variant (distilled 384-d) when int8 requested, or 2) postprocessing accidentally compressed/packed outputs. Need the response headers + request_id + serving logs.

Devon Eng: @Maria Support, ask for response headers and request_id (we set X-Model-Variant, X-Model-Id, X-Quant-Profile).

Maria Support: Customer pasted headers excerpt: 
```
X-Model-Id: open-embed-768-v1
X-Model-Variant: open-embed-384-distill
X-Quant-Profile: int8
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```

Maria Support: so routing returned open-embed-384-distill for that request.

Sophie DevEx: hmm why would routing map int8 -> distilled variant? We have compatibility rules but it should not change output dim.

Jules ML: looks like we introduced a low-memory distill alias for int8 paths recently — the compatibility table incorrectly marks the 384-distill as eligible for the 768 family when quant_profile=int8. I'll open a PR.

Devon Eng: also the customer reported big inference time: 
```
Request req_0a1b2c3d
- routing_time_ms: 12
- enqueue_ms: 18
- model_load_ms: 0 (hot)
- infer_compute_ms: 320  <-- expected ~40
- serialization_ms: 6
- total_ms: 360
```
Reverting to `fp16` gave ~45ms again. Could be runtime kernel fallback for int8.

Jules ML: yes, separate issue: if the tier doesn't have int8 CUDA kernels installed, runtime will try software/CPU fallback which kills latency and can 5xx under load. Two bugs: bad routing match + missing int8 kernels on that capacity.

Devon Eng: repro plan on staging: issue a batch with quant_profile=int8 and capture X-Model-Variant + router logs + runtime logs. I'll run now.

Ops Bot: rolling restart of model-router-v2 at 2026-03-15T09:02:00Z

Devon Eng: Ran curl on staging: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/sim/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-768-v1","input":["a","b","c"],"quant_profile":"int8","batch_size":8}'

Response headers:
X-Model-Id: open-embed-768-v1
X-Model-Variant: open-embed-384-distill
X-Quant-Profile: int8

Body: embedding vectors length=384
```

Jules ML: confirmed. Inspecting variant registry: compatibility row used `satisfies: low_memory` tag instead of `match_dim:true`. Distill variant was intended only for explicit requests of that model; routing wrongly allowed it as int8 fallback regardless of embedding_dim.

Maria Support: billing asked about credits. Carter Billing?

Carter Billing: we can give a one-time credit for failed runs in that window. Maria, collect request ids and times. I'll prepare a $300 credit pending engineering confirmation.

Devon Eng: runtime logs show that the capacity tier used did not have the int8 CUDA kernels for the model ops, so runtime fell back to a CPU quantized path which is much slower and can time out under heavy batching -> 5xx.

Jules ML: remediation plan: 
- hotfix router compatibility: enforce `match_dim` when selecting fallback variants (PR open).
- add request-time validation: check model metadata.embedding_dim == expected and return a 4xx with clear error if mismatch to avoid silent variant mapping.
- ops audit: ensure int8 kernels are installed on tiers that advertise int8 capability; if missing, soft-block int8 or advertise only fp16.

Sophie DevEx: also add a Console warning whenever a customer sets `quant_profile=int8` suggesting they verify GPU/kernel support or use Dedicated. And surface an "int8 support matrix" in docs.

Maria Support: customer applied temporary workaround: reverted to `fp16` and confirmed 768 dims + normal latency. They want timeline and whether int8 is supported at all.

Jules ML: int8 is supported for selected models and capacity tiers where kernels are available. We'll produce a short support doc and an internal matrix for which tiers have int8 kernels. Hotfix routing -> staging in ~30m, prod in ~2h after tests. Validation guardrail in ~6h. Ops audit 24-48h.

Devon Eng: I've attached repro logs and the failing request ids to ISSUE-EMB-987 and added an automated router log when X-Model-Variant differs from requested model base.

Oncall: added a monitor to alert when variant dimensionality != expected for a model family.

Maria Support: Draft customer reply: "Thanks for reporting — root cause: when `quant_profile=int8` our router incorrectly selected a distilled 384-d variant for your 768-d model, producing shorter vectors. Separately the int8 execution path on the capacity you used lacked optimized GPU kernels, causing CPU fallback -> higher latency and occasional 5xx. Temporary workaround: set `quant_profile=fp16` (keeps 768 dims) or use Dedicated capacity that supports int8. We're patching the routing rules, adding validation checks, and auditing kernel availability. We will issue a billing credit for affected runs (ISSUE-EMB-987). Sorry for the disruption."

Carter Billing: approved $300 credit; will follow up in ticket.

Ops Bot: ISSUE-EMB-987 routing fix deployed to prod at 2026-03-15T11:26:00Z

Maria Support: Patch live, customer confirmed resolution. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
